title: STEM BUILD LAB
tagline: Parts kids can actually build with — not a shopping mall
note: Start with controls and a Pi. Cabinets & coin doors come after a game works on a table.

categories.name: CONTROLS
categories.blurb: Hands on the game. Best first buy for a club lab.

items.name: Arcade joystick (8-way)
items.why: One stick + six buttons is a whole fighting or maze game.
items.tip: Sanwa / Seimitsu style or a solid clone. Mount in a control panel or a wooden box first.

items.name: Arcade buttons (30mm / 24mm)
items.why: Color-code lives, jump, and fire so kids can read the panel.
items.tip: Buy a mixed pack. Keep spares — buttons die from enthusiasm.

items.name: USB encoder (Zero Delay / GP2040)
items.why: Turns sticks and buttons into a gamepad the Pi or PC understands.
items.tip: GP2040-CE boards are worth it if you want clean mapping later.

items.name: Spinner / trackball
items.why: Arkanoid, Tempest, Centipede — games that need analog feel.
items.tip: Add after the standard stick panel works. One shared spinner is enough for a site.

categories.name: PIN / TABLES
categories.blurb: A pin table you can ship to a kiosk before anyone cuts wood.

items.name: Digital pinball table
items.why: Software table: flippers, nudge, drain, and a score reel. Kids learn timing and gravity without waiting on a cabinet.
items.tip: Build in MakeCode Arcade or p5.js. Left/right = flippers. Ball = circle + gravity. Drain = lose a ball. SUBMIT a playable link when it holds a ball for 30 seconds.

items.name: Flipper buttons (left / right)
items.why: Side buttons turn a stick panel into a pin table. Same encoder as the rest of the lab.
items.tip: Map two 30mm buttons to Left Shift / Right Shift or L1 / R1. Mount on the sides, not the top row.

categories.name: DANCE / RHYTHM
categories.blurb: Full-body input. Loud, obvious, and great for events.

items.name: Dance pad (USB or arcade tray)
items.why: Rhythm games pull kids who will not sit at a stick.
items.tip: Home USB pads are fine for testing. Arcade trays survive a Friday night.

items.name: Soft pad + foam underlay
items.why: Quiet practice pad for classrooms and after-school rooms.
items.tip: Tape edges. Floors eat cheap pads.

categories.name: RACING
categories.blurb: Wheels and pedals turn a table into a sit-down cab.

items.name: USB wheel + pedals
items.why: Outrun-style games and driving lessons without a full cabinet.
items.tip: Clamp to a table first. A fold-up racing seat is optional, not required.

items.name: Sit-down racing shell
items.why: Event piece. Looks like a real arcade, holds a wheel and a screen.
items.tip: Heavy. Plan transport and floor load before you buy a shell.

categories.name: COIN / TICKET
categories.blurb: How a machine takes money or tickets — or stays free-play.

items.name: Coin door + coin mech
items.why: Real arcade loop. Also the part most donated cabs are missing or jammed.
items.tip: Youth sites should default to free play. Use a mech only if the host wants fundraising credits.

items.name: Pulse / credit harness
items.why: Ties the door to the board or Pi so one coin = one credit.
items.tip: Label every wire. Future-you will not remember which pin is coin 1.

items.name: Ticket dispenser
items.why: Prize nights and carnival events.
items.tip: Only if the site can staff tickets. Otherwise it becomes a paper jam machine.

categories.name: BOARDS / HARNESS
categories.blurb: The original arcade brain — or the adapter that talks to one.

items.name: JAMMA harness
items.why: Standard plug for a huge pile of 80s/90s PCBs.
items.tip: Get a quality harness once. Cheap ones flake and take cabinets down.

items.name: Working PCB (donor board)
items.why: Repair class: trace a video issue, swap a RAM, learn the edge connector.
items.tip: Buy known-working first. Dead boards are a different class.

items.name: Isolation / switcher PSU
items.why: Arcade boards want +5 / +12. Wall warts do not.
items.tip: Measure voltages before you plug a rare board in.

categories.name: BRAINS (PI + KIOSK)
categories.blurb: Modern lab path. Same stack this site already runs on cabinets.

items.name: Raspberry Pi 4 / 5 (4GB+)
items.why: Emulation, kiosk browser, kid-made web games, attract mode.
items.tip: Official power supply. Cheap cables brown-out under a stick + screen.

items.name: Orange Pi / spare SBC
items.why: Cheaper second station so two kids can build at once.
items.tip: Match the image to the board. Not every Pi image boots on a clone.

items.name: Batocera / RetroPie image
items.why: Gets a stick talking to games in one evening.
items.tip: Legal dumps and homebrew only on charity floors.

items.name: Kiosk tablet (Onn / Galaxy Tab class)
items.why: Low-RAM terminals, sign-up, high scores, ArrrcadeOS in a cabinet bezel.
items.tip: Lock to the site. Kids will open YouTube if you leave a launcher.

categories.name: CABINET / SAFETY
categories.blurb: Wood, glass, power. Last — after the game runs on a bench.

items.name: Control panel blank + T-molding
items.why: Kids layout buttons on paper, then cut a real panel.
items.tip: Measure twice. A wrong 30mm hole is a very honest lesson.

items.name: Tempered glass / plexi bezel
items.why: Protects the screen on a live floor.
items.tip: Plexi for labs. Glass only if the cab is built for it.

items.name: Surge strip + metal ground
items.why: Wet floors and 40-year-old cabs do not mix.
items.tip: One fire extinguisher in the room. No daisy-chained power strips.

categories.name: PRINT / MAKE
categories.blurb: Custom parts the lab can iterate in an afternoon.

items.name: 3D-printed stick collar / button spacer
items.why: First useful print that goes on a real machine.
items.tip: PETG for shop parts. PLA is fine for prototypes.

items.name: Claw / ticket toy masters
items.why: Prize machines and event merch the kids designed.
items.tip: Keep wall thickness chunky. Tiny toys snap in a hopper.
